tasks.title: Add collection-owned route and authentication preparation
tasks.definition_of_done: ProviderCollection gains an additive async prepare_call contract whose registered route owns a concrete provider and AuthResolver. It validates one canonical provider:model Request, resolves authentication once, and returns an opaque PreparedProviderCall that privately freezes the request, selected provider, secret-bearing ResolvedAuth, and redacted route. Each sequential start_attempt reuses that frozen route/request/auth without re-resolution; at most one attempt is active, every attempt shares the frozen Request CancellationToken, cancellation terminates the call and forbids another attempt, and drop discards secrecy-wrapped auth without exposure. Credential rejection/expiry terminates the logical call; only explicit remediation plus user-level retry prepares again. ResolvedAuth carries closed non-secret AuthProvenance for static, environment, credential-store, and OAuth sources plus an allowed fallback reason. Missing routes, failed stored credentials or refresh, disallowed fallback, capability mismatch, request-route mismatch, and unsupported wire return typed errors without selecting another provider, model, credential policy, wire, or local implementation. Concrete opi-ai adapters implement the new prepared-auth attempt seam. The old stream(Request) path remains only as the explicit expand side for unmigrated workspace consumers until 17.5 removes it and resolver-bearing adapter state; 17.1 does not claim production cutover. Public opi-ai tests cover two-provider preparation, repeated attempts with one auth-resolution call, single-active-attempt enforcement, shared cancellation/no-post-cancel attempt, rejection/expiry termination, redacted drop/provenance/failures, and fixtures without adding a router trait, retry-factory trait, second registry, alias registry, provider breadth, or product policy.
